blocks.text: REACH.ai scans a salon’s live appointment book for last-minute openings and cancellations, then contacts customers by email or SMS to fill them.

Customers needed a brand new way to book those openings with the providers they know. As lead product designer, I built the booking experience from the ground up, aiming for a simple, enjoyable flow with less drop-off.
Users confirmed it was a success, and a 1-step SSO sign-in significantly reduced drop-off.

blocks.text: These customers want booking to be easy, on a regular cadence, and with the provider they already know. The experience had to handle every situation, whether they arrive by email or SMS, while keeping booking simple and cutting drop-off.

image.alt: Customer persona for the REACH.ai booking experience

items: Booking appointments far into the future
“I don’t want to think about booking”
Being placed with a different provider, with no rapport

blocks.text: I studied existing booking flows and UX patterns for last-minute reservations. Then I built sitemaps, content hierarchies, and navigation models so customers could find what they needed without friction.

items: Starting from zero: a brand new experience, so I mapped the information architecture before designing screens.
Every situation: customers arrive by email or SMS depending on their status, and one flow had to handle each case.
No metrics: real-time feedback and user testing guided each iteration.

image.alt: Booking experience sitemap and information architecture diagrams

blocks.text: Customers search by service or provider, so finding the right opening is quick.

blocks.text: A simple 3-step flow (find, review, confirm) keeps last-minute booking pleasant.

image.alt: Find, review, and confirm appointment screens

blocks.text: Users wanted to see a provider at a specific time, so we added a waitlist. After testing, it didn’t significantly impact bookings and was removed.

image.alt: Waitlist join, phone number, and confirmation screens

blocks.text: Simplifying sign-in to a single SSO step significantly reduced drop-off.

image.alt: One-time email link sign-in, error, and success states

blocks.text: Users confirmed the new booking platform was a success. Without metrics, we relied on real-time feedback and user testing to iterate and refine the design.
